profiles.use_case: Prepare a synthetic disposable cache plan, govern one refresh and a separately authorized teardown, then inspect retained records without repeating either occurrence.
synthetic_capabilities: Authoring, Standing inputs and the role digest are explicit local synthetic fixtures.
The cache target is a disposable Docker project and not a physical cache or production workload.
profiles.example_inputs: Caller-owned clean public source checkouts, exact regular-file executables, copied CPython environment, selected Docker/OpenSSL programs, a fresh synthetic runtime fixture root below /tmp, durable manager records and retained custody outside /tmp, and the published synthetic cache plan.
profiles.writer_requirement: One operator-owned disposable Docker host; a fresh absent synthetic runtime fixture root below /tmp; and a separate durable manager/control and retained-custody location outside /tmp. The selected Docker daemon remains a deployment trust boundary. Existing or uncertain roots must be inspected, not reused.
limitations: This is a finite attended local profile, not an installed service or general campaign runner.
The synthetic runtime fixture root must be below /tmp; /tmp is not a durable custody location.
A recorded result and settlement do not establish the cache condition later or authorize another effect.
The only supervisor-loss evidence is a scoped post-settlement interruption case; general resume and uncertain-action recovery are not established.
No production Standing service, independent reviewer, live human notification, external provider, federation or ECAD/design-flow workflow is included.

qualification.scope: public-only connected cache qualification with exact-result inspection, clean-release newcomer execution, pre-effect recovery checks and scoped post-settlement supervisor interruption
